reviews.comment: Caring person and clearly loves philosophy, just not the best at teaching it. He talks very quietly and doesn't explain things very well. He's very approachable if you have questions, which you will because no one ever knew what he was talking about. Grades are two exams, video presentations, in class presentations, and outside of class readings.
He's a decent professor. Talks quietly but likes what he does. Often likes to talk about his class being essential to learning to write. Skipping class is inconsequential to your grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He can be intimidating at first but I promise if you talk to him or ask him questions he's super nice. He can ramble a little but you would expect from a philosophy prof. I hate having to talk to profs but he's nice and understanding. His instructions can be unclear at times but he's usually not a very hard grader like you may expect. Talks quiet!
I took PHIL240 from him and it was pretty easy and he teaches the subject really well.

Sit in the very front so you can hear. In order to do well, you need to put in extra effort. Go over the book, attend the lecture, attend the help sessions, and make friends in your lab! If you need help, you'll typically be in contact with the PA instead of the professor, but I mean, it's a large class.

TAKE LITERALLY ANY OTHER MATH COURSE! Philosophy≠math, yet somehow Phil240 is considered a math course with absolutely no letters. He doesnt teach properly and honestly should retire. We learned more from the TA than from his lectures. The only thing that saved some people was the textbook, this shouldn't be taught as a 300+ people lecture.
Dr Raymond is a very kind professor who offers his students every chance to be successful
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The Canvas and lectures were confusing, and his handwriting was illegible at times. Labs were very helpful. Homework is extra credit on your final grade, and if you do better on the final than your final grade, it will replace the final grade!! He means well; he's just too knowledgeable to communicate it clearly.
Canvas was a mess. Spoke so quietly I sometimes couldn't hear even in the front. Illegible handwriting.

4 tests and final. Get an A in final get A in class. His class starts off strong and confusing, but the lab portion is very helpful. Lots of homework daily you could skimp on attendance in lecture and catch up in lab. He speaks very academically and knowledgeably about Logic so sometimes it's hard to keep up with him, but overall a good prof.

This class was a hot mess. Material was easy but he taught it poorly. I just stopped going to lectures entirely because i couldn't even hear him. His canvas page is a dumpster fire, and there are typos and errors all over assignments and even tests. His handwriting is possibly the worst I've ever seen.

He told me in front of 300+ students that my work on my test "made no sense" and was just a "big mess". The TA told me she "didn't have time for my questions" & the only time I met with Raymond outside of class he said I "lack a unique way of thinking" because I didn't understand the concepts that he was bad at teaching. He will embarrass you.
You either get it or you don't. It's a tough class but if it clicks then it is very possible to get an A. The homeworks are also completion grades and worth up to a letter grade of extra credit.

You get homework every day, but it really should only take you 10 minutes. Word of advice: if you don't go to class, you will not know what is going on. This is a challenging class, and it's tough to teach yourself. He is kind but very quiet, and it can be hard to understand him in this challenging class. For me, the TA helped me the most.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIM. The whole semester, nothing was uploaded to Canvas besides the homework. He was relatively accessible outside of class, but whenever you talked to him, he made it seem as if you did not know what you were learning. 60% of the grade came from exams that were not easy, 30% from the final, and the last 10% came from the lab. AVOID.

Do not get me wrong, this class is a VERY challenging class for the vast majority of students, you need to bring your A-game and cannot get behind. That being said, Dwayne does care that his students succeed and understands this course is challenging for most, just keep up with his work, you can get through it.

I had to drop this class because the textbook was very hard to navigate for me, and he speaks extremely quietly and doesn't use a microphone so I literally could not hear the lectures whatsoever. I personally wasn't able to schedule any time to meet with him and so I wasn't able to get ahold of the very difficult learning material in my head.

Generous with grading and scheduling, and very knowledgable in general—does a good job tying concepts together. Efficient course structure with homework due every night (for extra credit). The things you learn will help you beyond the scope of the class, especially if you have to take any proof-based math classes or argue with a sibling.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is very forgiving on grading and just wants you to succeed. Homework is very helpful, easy and quick to do, and is extra credit. So if you do all the homework, you get 10 points added to your final grade. He is also willing to help you as much as you need and is very forgiving.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Homework is due almost every night, but the assignments are fairly quick and easy. He is not good at planning ahead and changed exam dates multiple times which made things difficult for people taking their exams in the testing center. He does not respond to emails quickly if at all. He talks SUPER quiet and doesn't use the mic so sit at the front.
Dr. Raymond is one of the nicest professors you will ever meet! He helped me so much outside of class every week, and gives interesting lectures if you have read the material and are engaged!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Raymond is the sweetest man you'll ever meet. His a little monotoned but he clearly loves teaching and loves the topic. This man made his writing-intensive class to be exactly what it should be. He is very hard to listen to but he's a fair grader and he doesn't make the homework feel like homework. I actually look forward to doing his assignments.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not pay any attention to the bad reviews. Intro to logic is not hard, but there is a learning curve. Raymond is super accessible outside of class and will meet with you on zoom everyday and make sure you understand the content. He is quiet and his handwriting is messy, but other than that he is excellent. If you try, this class is an easy A
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: IGNORE THE BAD REVIEWS. Raymond was an incredibly intelligent professor. The material is a bit challenging at first but dont get discouraged! He is willing to help you outside of class so dont be scared/ intimidated to ask questions.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He writes on paper and then a camera projects what he's writing on the board. It is always blurry and hard to read especially with his messy handwriting. He's a nice guy and willing to help outside of class, but I gained almost nothing from going to class because of this, not to mention he talks so fast. If videos weren't posted I would've failed.

Dr. Raymond made this class extremely enjoyable. The material is a little hard to grasp at first but he goes above an beyond to make sure we understand it. There are SI sessions at least twice a week and he will zoom with anyone who needs help. He wants you to succeed in his class and the environment reflects that!

One of the most caring professors I've ever had. He makes the material so simple and easy, that if you go to the lectures and do the homework, you're pretty much getting an A in the class. Definitely take him if you can. This is your sign.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is so caring about every student learning the material, and will do whatever is needed to help you succeed! The material is tough, but the exams are so much easier than all the practice problems. He is so sweet and funny too!

Dont pay attention to all the bad reviews. Prof Raymond is challenging but he is SOOO worth it. Get him if you wish to ACTUALLY learn how to write or want to pursue graduate school. If you have a halfway decent attention span and wish to actually learn you will benefit in so many ways from his courses.

Loved this professor!! He is super willing to help you at anytime and even reaches out to ask if you need help. I would absolutely recommend taking him if you have the chance. Tests were take home, too, which was great for people that are stressed out test-takers. Also, has internship connections.

Professor Raymond clearly understands the material, but it seems like he isnt fantastic at teaching it. He just jumps from things way too fast for entry level symbolic logic. Half the time I feel like I am in an art class because I cannot read his super unorganized writing. But he does seem willing to offer a decent amount of outside help.
Okay but not great

50 minutes three times a week lets you get to know him well. the classes build and the tests are important to actually learn for the final. the test were easy after all the hw and minor studying. just do the hw right after class while it's on your mind and it's not every single day. i didn't use SI but my classmates really appreciated it.

Professor Raymond is a very nice guy, but should not be teaching. He's VERY smart but isn't the best at explaining things when asked questions. He takes forever to grade and lot of the grades in the class were participation, but instructions for most assignments were all over the place. Lacks organizational skills and made me SO stressed this fall.

This prof isn't as bad as everyone makes him seem. He's not the most interesting but he knows what he's talking about. His approach to logic is much more digestible than other PHIL240 profs I've seen. He assigns homework every day but it's technically extra credit, and the exams aren't too hard. The textbook is free and will be your best friend.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I totally get that online class is going to be more difficult than in-person due to the change in format, less personal classroom environment, etc. But Dr Raymond put in significantly less effort than any of my other profs, or it at least seems like it. Goes way too fast, doesn't answer questions clearly, and lectures are just hands on a screen.
He is so boring that I am writing this review during his class. I have never been so bored in my life.

Dont believe anyone who says you cant get an A in this class. If you go to most lectures and all labs, study, do your homework, and ask questions, I promise you can get an A. Your TA is your most valuable resource, go to them first for questions. The class is front-heavy, so if you put in the work at the beginning you should be fine.

Labs are mandatory, but class is optional. You'll learn everything he teaches in class in your lab, so hope you have a good TA. The TA is really who teaches you because Raymond just kinda talks over your head. Don't go to his office hours, ask your TA if you have any questions, just trust me on this one. Easy class.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Do not take this prof if you can help it. After the first test I completely stopped going to lectures because he made me more confused than if I just read the book. Go to lab because that's where you will actually learn and make sure you have a good TA. If you make a better grade on the final that will be your final grade in the class.

He goes too fast and is condescending with people who ask questions. He does not care about his students and will not respond to emails. Most people in his classes end up dropping. Material is hard and he makes it worse by skipping around the book and rushing through class. Halfway through the semester starting taking attendance randomly.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lab is really what matters in this class, attending lecture wasn't mandatory but could be helpful sometimes. Raymond really cares about his students though and felt we should all be able to get A's. Get the book, make sure you have a great lab TA, and ask questions. You'll do fine!

He spoke very quietly, mumbling, and skipping around. He wants students to come to lecture, but honestly it is not worth your time. Absolutely go to your lab, which is where you will actually learn. The prof does want you to eventually understand, so if your final grade is higher than your cumulative grade, he will give you your final grade.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is difficult on its own, but Professor Raymond isn't the greatest at explaining. He goes at a fast pace and doesn't really answer questions. You have to practice the material a lot in order to understand it, but the lab is really helpful. However, I suggest taking a different professor if you have to take this class.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Ok, Dr. Raymond is not the best. HOWEVER the subject matter itself is engaging and not hard to understand if you have a knack for it. Attendance isn't mandatory until no one starts showing up. He does a lot to make sure that the class passes, so rest assured there is extra credit (from homework and attendance) and curves on the tests.

This class was very overwhelming and professor Raymond did not help at all. His lectures are incredibly boring, and he can be quite condescending to students who do not understand the material. He also teaches at such a quick pace, but does not go in depth enough for you to understand. Overall don't recommend this class, especially with Raymond.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Nightmare of a class. Almost everyone who takes Logic from him ends up dropping the class. Goes through material much too fast and skips around in book so things aren't taught in the order they should be. He is condescending when speaking to students. If he is the only prof available, wait to take it with another prof. Not worth it at all
reviews.ratingTags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Definitely a doable course. The semester I took this course he replaces your final exam grade for your average if it's better than your entire average throughout the entire semester. You're going to use the textbook a lot for homework and for resources.

He is very boring and tough to understand in class. I attended every class but some students never went and taught themselves from the book. Labs are mandatory but are purely a grade boost. Awesome SI sessions that basically give you the exam ahead of time. The class definitely takes dedication but is doable.

Raymond is not good at explaining anything. He seems to be extremely smart in his field, but forgets his students do not know much. Lab is mandatory but will give you a letter grade boost at the end of the course if you keep up with hw. Lectures aren't mandatory really, pray you get a good TA and stick with the lab.

This course meets twice a week plus a 50 minute lab. Raymond goes fast in lecture and all of his lectures are repetitive. Attendance isn't taken, but good luck passing without going to lecture. Class is out of 110%, so go to lab and do homework for extra letter grade. Also, final exam grade will count as course grade if higher than weighted average
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Lectures aren't mandatory (or helpful). Go to your lab and do the homework. You'll learn best by reading the textbook, memorizing rules, and most importantly from T.A.s & going to help sessions! Dr. R speaks very quickly & quietly. class usually goes over people's heads. You'll need to put in work for your grade but it'll be ok. Lots of hwk.

Lectures aren't mandatory, mostly learn in lab. Do the homework in the textbooks, he sometimes takes test questions from there. Listen to your TA. Hard to understand in lecture, speaks quietly. Make a relationship with him. Be careful of small mistakes on exams, some cost 13+ points. Work for your grade for sure.

He was not a very good professor but the labs and the SI's will help you pass the class and make it interesting. It is not an easy, but if you put forth effort and do all the homework due in the labs you will pass.

If you're taking this in replacement of math, DONT. Class is not that difficult but he is a terrible professor who will not speak up in a lecture hall of 200+ students. He is very hard to approach. I went to his office hours and he was very condescending. Only place I learned anything is from the TA in lab.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class starts out really hard, but READ THE BOOK and go to lab and you'll be fine! The book tells you all of the material. Going to lecture is not needed to pass or even do well in this class. I found that my TA was much more help and was the reason I picked up the material.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: For those of you looking to take him as an alternative to math, this course IS DOABLE. You must be willing to learn, though. GO TO SI AND YOU WILL BE FINE. His knowledge of the material is so advanced, don't ask him questions- go to your SI or TA instead. Tests are easier than the homework, so don't be intimidated. Course gets easier throughout.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Took in Spring 2015. Most difficult "math" course. Lectures were long and boring, the material was not easily explained. Soft-spoken even with mic. Schedules meetings during his office hours so he's not available until right before the class. Does not respond to emails. TA's are important resources--USE THEM!!! Practice, Practice, PRACTICE!!!
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lectures are very dry and hard to understand. He is also very soft spoken and doesn't answer questions. He is a very nice guy, but not very helpful. I learned the most from my TA in lab and from the SI sessions.

I learned most of the material in lab with my TA. Dr. Raymond is good at presenting an overview of the material but the TAs are the ones who really answer questions and slow things down so you can understand what is going on. The material can be confusing at the beginning but there are lots of help sessions and practice problems available to help.

This can be a really easy class if you put the necessary effort in.  Definitely keep up with the chapters that you're covering in the textbook. There's plenty of help available if you need it. The lectures themselves aren't really that helpful, I learned more from the SI sessions and reading the book on my own than I did from going to lecture.

Honestly I didn't learn a thing by going to lecture. He mumbles a lot when he talks and he kinda goes all over the place. GO TO SI's AND LAB!!!!!! They literally saved my grade in this class. There's no quizzes and 5 tests including the final. The good news if you fail every test but make an A on the final, he'll put an A as your course grade.

Sit in front row.  He refuses to wear the microphone in an auditorium built for a capacity of about 400 students.  When asked to speak up he refuses but tells you to move to the front row.  DON'T listen to what you are told about being raised a full letter grade by participating and showing up for all of the labs -- FALSE.  Read the syllabus only!

The class is not really hard, it's just the way the grades are structured that makes the class seem difficult. There are two essays that he grades very strictly and then a final and a midterm that are very easy. Dr. Raymond will help with any questions if you ask but it's just really important to read the material that he assigns.

Very easy class. Go to lectures and labs, and then practice practice practice on your own and you will get the material. Labs offer a ton of help to succeed. Made a 100 in the class, highly suggest taking it over math. Dr. Raymond is awesome as well. I loved his lectures; he is absolutely brilliant and fun to listen to.

There were four tests, including the final. There was up to 5 points in extra credit from attending labs. He takes the higher of the following two grades: 1) your average test grade plus bonus, 2) your grade on the final. Yes, you can fail every test but if you get an A on the final, then you get an A in the class.  Go to the labs!

Grades consist of 2 papers, which he graded strictly, and 2 tests, which were short answer, but very easy. Lectures were either slide or discussion based. His class was very disorganized and he didn't do a very good job explaining what we were supposed to do for the paper. He is pretty lenient though. Also, sit up close, he has a very quiet voice.

Raymond is a very smart man, but his lectures are hard to follow, he easily becomes frustrated with you if you don't understand what he's saying. The class offers a lot of extra credit outside class, but lectures are just kinda confusing. His handwriting is awful too. Go to the SI sessions! They really help. But overall it's not hard to get an A!

Class is interesting, but the material can be hard to follow. Professor is really cool and down to earth, and always willing to help. Lots of help in the labs but you have to be willing to practice the material outside of class. I would definitely take another one of his classes. He holds drop in sessions for extra help and cares about students.

You can tell that he loves the subject and sometimes will talk as if we all know what's going on, but he's such a nice guy. Reading the material is pretty crucial to understanding. The labs are literally perfect for help, Andrew Soto was my TA and he helped me SO much. Just pay attention and don't be afraid to ask questions and you'll be fine.

He never goes over new concepts during lecture but the lessons are super helpful if you're kind of confused or need extra help. The TAs do most of the actual teaching, but mine was really great! There is so much extra help available for this class.
Really difficult to follow. You learn more from the lab sessions

Excellent and extremely helpful professor. Explain with clarity and as long as one follows along with class and does the assingments and PRACTICES SUFFICIENTLY, they should do well in the class. Would definitely recommend no-one else. Very nice and friendly especially in office hours.
